# mzmlpy — full usage guide for AI assistants

> mzmlpy is a lightweight, type-safe, lazy-loading Python library (3.12+) for reading mzML mass
> spectrometry files, including gzip-compressed `.mzML.gz`. Only `numpy` is required at runtime.
> This file is a self-contained reference for writing correct mzmlpy code. It matches the public
> API of version 0.9.1; every name and signature below was checked by importing it.

Docs site: https://tacular-omics.github.io/mzmlpy/ · Source: https://github.com/tacular-omics/mzmlpy ·
PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/mzmlpy/

## Install

```bash
pip install mzmlpy
# optional decoders and features (imported lazily, only when needed):
pip install "mzmlpy[numpress]"    # MS-Numpress arrays (pynumpress>=0.1.5)
pip install "mzmlpy[zstd]"        # Zstandard-compressed arrays
pip install "mzmlpy[rapidgzip]"   # seekable .mzML.gz without extracting (gzip_mode="indexed")
pip install "mzmlpy[mcp]"         # local MCP server (python -m mzmlpy mcp)
```

Opening a file never needs an extra. Decoding an array that uses Numpress or zstd without the
extra raises an error naming the extra to install.

## Quick start

Always use the context manager so file handles are closed.

```python
from mzmlpy import Mzml

with Mzml("run.mzML") as reader:
    print(reader.file_name, len(reader.spectra), "spectra")
    for spectrum in reader.spectra:
        mz = spectrum.mz                 # np.ndarray | None, decoded now
        intensity = spectrum.intensity
        if mz is not None:
            print(spectrum.id, f"MS{spectrum.ms_level}", len(mz), "peaks")
```

Check many files cheaply without building an index:

```python
from mzmlpy import peek_spectrum_count

n = peek_spectrum_count("run.mzML.gz")   # int | None; reads only up to <spectrumList count=...>
```

## The reader: `Mzml`

```python
Mzml(
    file: str | Path | BinaryIO,          # path, or a readable binary file-like object (e.g. BytesIO)
    *,                                    # everything else is keyword-only
    build_index_from_scratch: bool = False,  # ignore the file's <indexList> and rebuild offsets
    gzip_mode: Literal["auto", "extract", "indexed", "stream"] = "auto",
    in_memory: bool = True,               # load the whole (decompressed) file into memory
    extract_dir: str | Path | None = None,   # where gzip_mode="extract" writes; default <tmpdir>/mzmlpy/
    spectrum_id_regex: str | None = None,    # secondary lookup key for spectra (first capture group)
    chromatogram_id_regex: str | None = None,
)
```

A non-path object without `read`/`readline` raises `TypeError`.

Reader properties and methods:

| member | type | purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `spectra` | `SpectrumLookup` | index / id / slice / iterate / filter spectra |
| `chromatograms` | `ChromatogramLookup` | same for chromatograms |
| `total_ion_chromatogram` | `Chromatogram \| None` | total ion chromatogram (by id `"TIC"` or CV term MS:1000235) |
| `id` | `str` | mzML `id` attribute |
| `version` | `str` | mzML version string, e.g. `"1.1.0"` |
| `file_name` | `str` | file name |
| `file_path` | `Path \| None` | path, if opened from a path or a named file object |
| `access_strategy` | `AccessStrategy` | backend chosen at open (see below) |
| `file_description` | `FileDescription \| None` | `<fileDescription>` |
| `run` | `Run \| None` | `<run>` attributes |
| `instrument_configurations` | `dict[str, InstrumentConfiguration]` | keyed by id |
| `softwares` | `dict[str, Software]` | keyed by id |
| `samples` | `dict[str, Sample]` | keyed by id |
| `data_processes` | `dict[str, DataProcessing]` | keyed by id |
| `scan_settings` | `dict[str, ScanSetting]` | keyed by id |
| `referenceable_param_groups` | `dict[str, ReferenceableParamGroup]` | keyed by id |
| `obo_version` | `str \| None` | PSI-MS CV version declared in `<cvList>` (read-only) |
| `cvs` | `dict[str, CVElement]` | controlled vocabularies (`CVElement(id, full_name, version, uri)`) |
| `validate(*, decode_binary=False, check_index=False)` | `ValidationReport` | validate through a fresh handle; open iterators are unaffected |
| `close()` | `None` | close the file (done by the context manager) |

Every dict property returns a new dict on each call. Header metadata is parsed when the reader opens. Spectra and chromatograms are read and parsed
only when accessed.

### `AccessStrategy` (StrEnum)

`reader.access_strategy` reports the storage backend actually used:

| value | when |
|---|---|
| `memory` | `in_memory=True` (the default), any input; also `BytesIO` input |
| `plain` | uncompressed file with `in_memory=False` |
| `embedded` | self-indexed gzip written by `write_indexed_gzip`, `in_memory=False` |
| `extracted` | `.gz` decompressed to a cache file (`gzip_mode="extract"`, or `"auto"` fallback) |
| `rapidgzip` | `gzip_mode="indexed"` (needs the `rapidgzip` extra) |
| `stream` | `gzip_mode="stream"`: sequential only |

## Lookups: `SpectrumLookup`, `ChromatogramLookup`

```python
reader.spectra[0]              # by 0-based index; negative indices count from the end
reader.spectra["scan=19"]      # by native id (MzmlRecordNotFoundError, a KeyError, if absent)
reader.spectra[0:5]            # slice -> list[Spectrum]
len(reader.spectra)            # count (0 for an empty file, does not raise)
"scan=19" in reader.spectra    # membership by id
for s in reader.spectra: ...   # iterate in file order, memory-bounded
```

Methods (both lookups):

- `get_by_index(index: int) -> T`: same as `lookup[index]`; a non-int raises `TypeError`.
- `get_by_id(identifier: str) -> T`: same as `lookup["id"]`.
- `get_by_slice(slice_obj: slice) -> list[T]`
- `count -> int | None`: declared record count.
- `SpectrumLookup.filter(*, ms_level=None, rt=None, polarity=None, precursor_mz=None,
  spectrum_type=None, mobility_type=None, ion_mobility=None, faims_voltage=None) -> Iterator[Spectrum]`:
  lazy metadata selection (see Filtering).

### Look up by scan number with `id_regex`

```python
# The first capture group (or the full match if no groups) becomes a secondary key.
with Mzml("run.mzML", spectrum_id_regex=r"scan=(\d+)") as reader:
    s = reader.spectra["19"]     # instead of "controllerType=0 controllerNumber=1 scan=19"
```

`chromatogram_id_regex` works the same way for chromatograms. The full native id keeps working.

## `Spectrum`

All properties are lazy and return `None` (or `()` for sequences) when the term is absent.

| property | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `str` | native id, e.g. `"controllerType=0 controllerNumber=1 scan=1"` |
| `id_dict` | `dict[str, int \| str]` | native id split into `key=value` parts, e.g. `{"scan": 19}` |
| `index` | `int \| None` | the XML `index` attribute |
| `default_array_length` | `int \| None` | number of points |
| `mz` | `np.ndarray \| None` | decoded m/z array (decoded on every access) |
| `intensity` | `np.ndarray \| None` | decoded intensity array |
| `charge_array` | `np.ndarray \| None` | per-point charge array, if present |
| `ms_level` | `int \| None` | 1, 2, ... |
| `polarity` | `Literal["positive", "negative"] \| None` | |
| `spectrum_type` | `Literal["centroid", "profile"] \| None` | |
| `spectra_combination` | `Literal["no_combination", "median", "sum", "mean"] \| None` | scanList combination term |
| `rt` | `float \| None` | retention time in seconds, from the first scan (warns if there are several) |
| `ion_injection_time` | `float \| None` | milliseconds, from the first scan (warns if there are several) |
| `mz_range` | `tuple[float, float] \| None` | scan-window envelope (min lower, max upper) of the first scan |
| `filter_string` | `str \| None` | instrument filter string (e.g. Thermo) |
| `ook0` | `float \| None` | scan-level 1/K0 (MS:1002815) of the first scan |
| `ion_mobility` | `float \| None` | scan-level 1/K0 (preferred) or drift time |
| `has_im` | `bool` | ion mobility present (array or scan term) |
| `im_types` | `set[BinaryDataArrayAccession]` | ion-mobility array types present |
| `total_ion_current` | `float \| None` | total ion current of this spectrum (MS:1000285) |
| `base_peak_mz` / `base_peak_intensity` | `float \| None` | MS:1000504 / MS:1000505 |
| `lowest_observed_mz` / `highest_observed_mz` | `float \| None` | MS:1000528 / MS:1000527 |
| `scans` | `tuple[Scan, ...]` | scan list |
| `is_single_scan` | `bool` | exactly one scan |
| `precursors` | `tuple[Precursor, ...]` | MSn precursor info; `has_precursors: bool` |
| `products` | `tuple[Product, ...]` | product list; `has_products: bool` |
| `binary_arrays` | `tuple[BinaryDataArray, ...]` | all arrays |
| `data_processing_ref`, `source_file_ref`, `spot_id` | `str \| None` | XML attributes |

Methods: `get_binary_array(id: str) -> BinaryDataArray | None` and `has_binary_array(id: str) -> bool`
take an array accession or name (e.g. `"MS:1000514"` / `"m/z array"`).

### Precursors, products, scans

```python
for prec in spectrum.precursors:
    win = prec.isolation_window           # IsolationWindow | None
    if win is not None:
        win.target_mz, win.lower_offset, win.upper_offset   # float | None
    for ion in prec.selected_ions:        # tuple[SelectedIon, ...]
        ion.mz, ion.charge, ion.intensity
    act = prec.activation                 # Activation | None
    if act is not None:
        act.activation_type               # CollisionDissociationTypeAccession | None, e.g. CID MS:1000133
        act.collision_energy              # MS:1000045, eV, float | None
    prec.spectrum_ref                     # id of the precursor spectrum, str | None

for prod in spectrum.products:
    prod.isolation_window                 # IsolationWindow | None (also has .no_isolation: bool)
```

- `Precursor`: `isolation_window`, `selected_ions`, `activation`, `spectrum_ref`,
  `external_spectrum_id`, `source_file_ref`.
- `SelectedIon`: `mz`, `charge`, `intensity`, `ook0` (1/K0),
  `drift_time`, `ccs`, `faims_voltage_start`, `faims_voltage_end`.
- `Activation`: `activation_type`, `collision_energy`, `supplemental_collision_energy`, `activation_energy`, `collision_gas`,
  `collision_gas_pressure`.
- `IsolationWindow`: `target_mz`, `lower_offset`, `upper_offset`, `mz_range`, `no_isolation` (MS:1003159).
- `Product`: `isolation_window`.
- `Scan`: `rt` (float seconds), `ion_injection_time` (float ms), `filter_string`,
  `scan_windows: tuple[ScanWindow, ...]`, `is_single_windowed_scan`, `mz_range` (envelope of all windows),
  `ook0` (MS:1002815), `drift_time` (MS:1002476),
  `faims_compensation_voltage` (MS:1001581), `selexion_separation_voltage` (MS:1003394),
  `selexion_compensation_voltage` (MS:1003371).
- `ScanWindow`: `lower_mz`, `upper_mz`, `mz_range`.

## `Chromatogram`

```python
with Mzml("run.mzML") as reader:
    tic = reader.total_ion_chromatogram   # Chromatogram | None
    for chrom in reader.chromatograms:
        t = chrom.time                    # np.ndarray | None (time array in its recorded unit)
        i = chrom.intensity
        chrom.chromatogram_type           # "tic", "sic", "srm", "basepeak", ... or None
    sic = reader.chromatograms["sic"]     # by id
```

Properties: `id`, `id_dict`, `time`, `intensity`, `chromatogram_type`
(`Literal["emission", "sim", "basepeak", "pic", "tic", "absorption", "srm", "sic"] | None`),
`precursor: Precursor | None`, `product: Product | None`, `has_precursor`, `has_product`,
`binary_arrays`, `default_array_length`, `data_processing_ref`, `source_file_ref`.
Methods: `get_binary_array(id)`, `has_binary_array(id)`.

## `BinaryDataArray`

| member | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | `np.ndarray` | decode and return the array (not cached) |
| `binary_array_type` | `BinaryDataArrayAccession \| None` | m/z, intensity, ion mobility, ... |
| `encoding` | `BinaryDataTypeAccession \| None` | 32/64-bit float or int |
| `compression` | `CompressionTypeAccession \| None` | zlib, zstd, Numpress variants, none |

## CV parameter access (every record and metadata wrapper)

`Spectrum`, `Chromatogram`, `Scan`, `Precursor`, `BinaryDataArray`, `FileContent`,
`InstrumentConfiguration`, `Software`, `Sample`, etc. share these helpers:

- `get_cv_param(id: str) -> CvParam | None`: by accession (`"MS:1000511"`) or name (`"ms level"`).
- `has_cv_param(id: str) -> bool`
- `cv_float(id: str) -> float | None`, `cv_int(id: str) -> int | None`: numeric value; raises
  `MzmlError` (a `ValueError`) naming the term if the value is not numeric.
- `cv_params -> tuple[CvParam, ...]`, `accessions -> frozenset[str]`, `names -> frozenset[str]`
- `user_params -> tuple[UserParam, ...]`, `get_user_param(name)`, `has_user_param(name)`
- `ref_params -> tuple[ReferenceableParamGroupRef, ...]`, `get_ref_param(ref)`, `has_ref_param(ref)`
- `get_attribute(attr_name: str) -> str | None`: raw XML attribute.
- `serialize() -> dict[str, object]`: full element content as nested dicts (a fresh copy).

`CvParam(name, value, unit_accession, unit_name, unit_cv_ref, cv_ref, accession)` and
`UserParam(name, value, unit_accession, unit_name, unit_cv_ref, type_value)` are frozen
dataclasses; both have `to_timedelta -> timedelta | None` for time-unit values.
`ReferenceableParamGroupRef(ref)` and `SourceFileRef(ref)` hold a referenced id.

Referenceable parameter groups are expanded in place, so a term defined in a
`<referenceableParamGroup>` is found by `get_cv_param` on the element that references it.

```python
spec = reader.spectra[0]
spec.get_cv_param("MS:1000511").value      # "1" (str | None)
spec.cv_int("MS:1000511")                # 1
spec.has_cv_param("centroid spectrum")
```

## Header metadata classes

- `FileDescription`: `file_content: FileContent | None`, `source_files: tuple[SourceFile, ...]`,
  `get_source_file(id) -> SourceFile | None`, `contact: tuple[Contact, ...]`.
- `FileContent`: CV terms for the file's content; `is_dia: bool` (a merged DIA method term is
  declared), `dia_acquisition: DIAAcquisitionAccession | None`.
- `SourceFile`: `id`, `name`, `location`, `checksum`, `checksum_type` (`"MD5" | "SHA1" | "SHA256" | None`).
- `Contact`: `name`, `organization`, `address`, `email`, `url`, `role`, `phone_number`,
  `fax_number`, `toll_free_phone_number`.
- `InstrumentConfiguration`: `id`, `software_ref`, `source_components`, `analyzer_components`,
  `detector_components` (tuples of `SourceComponent` / `AnalyzerComponent` / `DetectorComponent`,
  each with `order: int | None` plus CV terms).
- `Software`: `id`, `version`.
- `Sample`: `id`, `name`.
- `Run`: `id`, `start_time_stamp: datetime | None`, `default_instrument_configuration_ref`,
  `default_source_file_ref`, `sample_ref`.
- `DataProcessing`: `id`, `processing_methods: tuple[ProcessingMethod, ...]`.
- `ProcessingMethod`: `order: int | None`, `software_ref: str | None`, plus CV terms.
- `ScanSetting`: `id`, `source_file_refs: tuple[SourceFileRef, ...]`, `targets: tuple[Target, ...]`.
- `Target`: `mz: float | None`.
- `ReferenceableParamGroup`: `id` plus CV/user params.

```python
with Mzml("run.mzML") as reader:
    for cfg in reader.instrument_configurations.values():
        print(cfg.id, [a.names for a in cfg.analyzer_components])
    for sw in reader.softwares.values():
        print(sw.id, sw.version)
    if reader.run is not None:
        print(reader.run.start_time_stamp)
    fc = reader.file_description.file_content if reader.file_description else None
    print(fc.is_dia if fc else None)
```

## Filtering (metadata only, lazy)

```python
with Mzml("run.mzML") as reader:
    for s in reader.spectra.filter(ms_level=2, rt=(60, 180), polarity="positive"):
        print(s.id)
```

`SpectrumFilter(*, ms_level=None, rt=None, polarity=None, precursor_mz=None,
spectrum_type=None, mobility_type=None, ion_mobility=None, faims_voltage=None)` is the same
predicate as a frozen, keyword-only dataclass; `SpectrumFilter(...).matches(spectrum) -> bool`.

- Criteria combine with AND. Range criteria are `(low, high)` tuples, inclusive, either end may be `None`.
- `rt` is in **seconds**, matched against any scan's start time.
- `precursor_mz` matches isolation-window overlap, falling back to selected-ion m/z.
- `ion_mobility` requires `mobility_type="inverse_reduced"` or `"drift_time"` and uses the
  recorded scan value in its declared unit. `faims_voltage` is signed volts.
- Missing metadata never matches. Filtering never decodes binary arrays.

## Validation

```python
from mzmlpy import validate

report = validate("run.mzML.gz", decode_binary=False, check_index=False)
report.valid          # parsing completed and no error-severity issues
report.complete       # parsing reached the end of the document
for issue in report.issues:
    print(issue.severity, issue.code, issue.location, issue.message)
report.to_dict()      # JSON-serializable, includes "valid"
```

- `validate(file: str | Path, *, decode_binary=False, check_index=False) -> ValidationReport`.
  Works on plain and gzip mzML and never creates or repairs caches.
- `ValidationReport` fields: `issues: tuple[ValidationIssue, ...]`, `spectrum_count`,
  `chromatogram_count`, `arrays_decoded`, `index_entries_checked`, `complete`, `decode_binary`,
  `check_index`; property `valid`; method `to_dict()`.
- `ValidationIssue(code, message, location, severity="error" | "warning")`. Codes include
  `count_mismatch`, `duplicate_id`, `missing_id`, `missing_reference`, `invalid_integer`,
  `unsupported_or_missing_encoding`, `unsupported_or_missing_compression`, `missing_binary`.
- `decode_binary=True` decodes every array and checks lengths; `check_index=True` verifies the
  `<indexList>` offsets. Full XSD and ontology validation are out of scope.
- `reader.validate(...)` does the same for an open reader.

## Gzipped files (`.mzML.gz`)

```python
Mzml("run.mzML.gz")                                          # default: decompress into memory
Mzml("run.mzML.gz", gzip_mode="extract", in_memory=False)    # decompress to a cache file, then random access
Mzml("run.mzML.gz", gzip_mode="indexed", in_memory=False)    # rapidgzip seekable access (needs extra)
Mzml("run.mzML.gz", gzip_mode="stream", in_memory=False)     # lowest startup; random access rescans (slow, warns)
```

- `gzip_mode` only matters with `in_memory=False`. With the default `in_memory=True` the whole
  decompressed file is buffered and every mode behaves the same.
- `"auto"` uses, in order: an embedded index (self-indexed gzip), a current extracted cache,
  complete rapidgzip sidecars; otherwise it extracts.
- `"extract"` caches under `<tmpdir>/mzmlpy/` unless `extract_dir` is given. Cache files are
  reused only while the source's path, size and timestamps are unchanged.
- `"indexed"` writes index sidecars next to the source (`run.mzML.gzidx`, `run.mzMLidx` and
  `.src` signature files), so that directory must be writable.
- `clear_cache() -> None` deletes `<tmpdir>/mzmlpy/` (it does not touch `extract_dir` or sidecars).

### Self-indexed gzip (pyMZML-compatible)

```python
from mzmlpy import write_indexed_gzip, is_embedded_indexed_gzip

result = write_indexed_gzip("run.mzML", "run.mzML.gz", compression_level=6)
result.output_path, result.spectrum_count, result.chromatogram_count, result.member_count, result.index_entry_count
is_embedded_indexed_gzip("run.mzML.gz")   # True

with Mzml("run.mzML.gz", in_memory=False) as reader:   # access_strategy == "embedded"
    reader.spectra[1000]                                # random access, no extraction
```

- `write_indexed_gzip(source, output, *, compression_level=6) -> IndexedGzipWriteResult`:
  deterministic output; `index_gzip` is the same function under another name.
- `is_embedded_indexed_gzip(path) -> bool`: checks for the pyMZML `FU` version-1 marker.
- The output is still a normal gzip file that any gzip reader can decompress.

## Command line

```bash
python -m mzmlpy inspect run.mzML                     # JSON: file, id, version, access_strategy, counts
python -m mzmlpy validate run.mzML.gz --decode-binary --check-index   # JSON report
python -m mzmlpy index-gzip run.mzML run.mzML.gz      # JSON IndexedGzipWriteResult
python -m mzmlpy mcp --root /abs/data [--output-dir /abs/exports]      # MCP server on stdio
```

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 invalid data (validate), 2 operational error (message on stderr).

## MCP server (optional, `mzmlpy[mcp]`)

```bash
pip install "mzmlpy[mcp]"
python -m mzmlpy mcp --root /absolute/path/to/data
```

Client configuration:

```json
{"mcpServers": {"mzmlpy": {"command": "/abs/venv/bin/python",
  "args": ["-m", "mzmlpy", "mcp", "--root", "/abs/data"]}}}
```

- Programmatic: `from mzmlpy.mcp import create_server; create_server(root, output_dir=None).run(transport="stdio")`.
- 17 tools by default: `server_info`, `list_files`, `inspect_file`, `get_metadata`,
  `summarize_run`, `compare_runs`, `validate_file`, `find_spectra`, `get_spectrum`, `get_spectra`,
  `list_chromatograms`, `get_chromatogram`, `get_array`, `start_job`, `get_job`, `cancel_job`,
  `release_job`. With `--output-dir`, also `export_records` and `read_export` (JSONL with original
  binary encodings).
- Resources: `mzmlpy://capabilities`, `mzmlpy://guide`, `mzmlpy://units`, `mzmlpy://schemas`.
- Read-only: sources are never modified; paths must resolve inside `--root`; no caches or
  sidecars are created. Times are seconds. Results carry `file`, `revision`, `data`; continue
  paging with `next_index`, unchanged filters and `expected_revision`.
- Integers outside `[-(2**53-1), 2**53-1]` are sent as exact decimal strings.
- No spectrum processing or plotting (that belongs to spxtacular / visualization clients).
- Full reference: https://tacular-omics.github.io/mzmlpy/mcp/

## Constants (`mzmlpy.constants`)

CV accessions are `StrEnum`s (compare with the enum or with the accession string):
`BinaryDataArrayAccession`, `BinaryDataTypeAccession`, `CompressionTypeAccession`,
`SpectrumMSAccession`, `ChromatogramTypeAccession`, `CollisionDissociationTypeAccession`,
`IsolationWindowAccession`, `SelectedIonAccession`, `ActivationAccession`,
`DIAAcquisitionAccession`, `SpectrumCombinationAccession`, `ChecksumTypeAccession`,
`ContactAccession`, `TimeUnitAccession`, `SpectrumTypeAccession`, `ScanPolarity`, plus `ION_MOBILITIES`
(frozenset of ion-mobility array accessions).

```python
from mzmlpy.constants import BinaryDataArrayAccession

arr = spectrum.get_binary_array(BinaryDataArrayAccession.MZ)   # same as "MS:1000514"
```

## Numeric types

- Decoded arrays keep their declared dtype (float32, float64, int32, int64), also when empty.
- Numpress arrays reconstruct as float64; no further narrowing.
- Arrays are writable and freshly decoded on each access. Convert explicitly when you need a
  type: `spectrum.mz.astype(np.float64)`. Integer arithmetic on int32 arrays can overflow.
- `rt` is a float in seconds and `ion_injection_time` a float in milliseconds, both converted from
  the recorded unit. A missing or non-time unit is taken as seconds (ms for injection time) and
  warns once per unit; a non-numeric value raises `MzmlError`. `chrom.time` is the raw array in its recorded unit.

## Worked examples

MS2 precursor table:

```python
from mzmlpy import Mzml

rows = []
with Mzml("run.mzML") as reader:
    for s in reader.spectra.filter(ms_level=2):
        rt = s.rt  # seconds, or None
        for p in s.precursors:
            for ion in p.selected_ions:
                rows.append((s.id, rt, ion.mz, ion.charge))
```

Base-peak chromatogram from MS1 spectra (computed by you, not stored in the file):

```python
import numpy as np
from mzmlpy import Mzml

times, bpis = [], []
with Mzml("run.mzML.gz", gzip_mode="extract", in_memory=False) as reader:
    for s in reader.spectra.filter(ms_level=1):
        intensity = s.intensity
        if intensity is not None and len(intensity) and s.rt is not None:
            times.append(s.rt)
            bpis.append(float(intensity.max()))
```

timsTOF ion mobility:

```python
with Mzml("bruker.mzML") as reader:
    s = reader.spectra[0]
    if s.has_im:
        print(s.ion_mobility, s.im_types)   # scan-level 1/K0 and per-point mobility arrays present
```

Validate a batch of files:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from mzmlpy import validate

for path in Path("data").glob("*.mzML*"):
    report = validate(path)
    print(path.name, report.valid, len(report.issues))
```

## Gotchas / rules for correct code

- **Decoding is not cached.** `spectrum.mz` / `.intensity` decode on every access. Assign once:
  `mz = spectrum.mz`.
- **Not thread-safe.** A reader shares one file handle; use one `Mzml` per thread or process.
- **Absence is `None`.** `polarity`, `ms_level`, `mz`, `total_ion_current`, `rt`, ... can be `None`.
  Always guard. Empty arrays can be `None` or length 0.
- **Warnings, not exceptions**, for ambiguous cases: a spectrum with several scans warns and
  returns the first scan's value for `rt`, `mz_range`, etc. Missing or assumed
  compression/data-type terms also warn.
- **Retention time units**: `rt` and filter bounds are seconds; `Chromatogram.time` is the raw array in its recorded unit (check its unit CV term).
- **`gzip_mode="stream"` is for one sequential pass.** Indexing into it rescans from the start.
- **Use the context manager** (`with Mzml(...) as reader:`) or call `reader.close()`.
- **Ids are strings.** `reader.spectra["19"]` only works with `spectrum_id_regex`; `reader.spectra[19]`
  is the 20th spectrum by position, not scan 19. Use `s.id_dict["scan"]` for the scan number.

## Exceptions

All in `mzmlpy` (and `mzmlpy.errors`):

- `MzmlError(ValueError)`: base for bad data or bad arguments; `except ValueError` still works.
- `MzmlParseError`: empty, malformed, truncated or non-mzML XML (wraps `ParseError` as `__cause__`).
- `MzmlOffsetIndexError`: an offset index (indexList, cached or embedded gzip index) disagrees with the file.
- `MzmlDecodeError`: a binary array cannot be decoded.
- `MzmlRecordNotFoundError(MzmlError, KeyError)`: no record with that id.
- Integer index out of range raises `IndexError`; wrong argument types raise `TypeError`.

## Error messages you may see

- `Decoding this array requires the optional 'pynumpress' package … pip install mzmlpy[numpress]`
  → install the named extra (same for `zstd`, `rapidgzip`).
- `Cannot decode binary array: N bytes is not a multiple of the M-byte element size …`
  → corrupt or truncated array, or an unsupported truncation encoding.
- `CV param '<name>' (MS:xxxx) has a non-numeric value '<value>'` → malformed value in the file.
- `Failed to base64-decode binary data array …` → corrupt `<binary>` content.
- `Unsupported input type 'int': expected a path (str/Path) or a readable binary file-like object.`
  → pass a path or an open binary file.

## Changelog highlights

- 0.10.0: breaking API cleanup (`rt`, `ook0`, `mz_range`, `collision_energy`, `MzmlError`
  hierarchy; see the migration guide: https://tacular-omics.github.io/mzmlpy/migration/).
- 0.9.1: `numpress` extra requires `pynumpress>=0.1.5` (wheels on macOS/Windows).
- 0.9.0: optional MCP server; decoded arrays keep their native dtype (previously float64).
- 0.8.0: `validate`, `SpectrumFilter` / `spectra.filter`, `python -m mzmlpy` CLI, self-indexed gzip.

Full history: https://github.com/tacular-omics/mzmlpy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
